prompt: In Ohio, it is illegal for a driver 21 or older to drive with a blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) at or above what level?
explanation: Ohio law prohibits driving with a BAC of .08% or higher at any age. Lower limits apply to commercial drivers (.04%) and drivers under 21 (.02%).
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: What is the BAC limit for Ohio drivers under age 21?
explanation: Drivers under 21 break Ohio law at a BAC of .02% or higher, a much lower limit than the .08% that applies to all drivers.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: Under Ohio law, a commercial driver may not drive with a BAC at or above:
explanation: Ohio sets a .04% BAC limit for commercial drivers, half the .08% limit that applies at any age.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: A 19-year-old Ohio driver is stopped and tests at .03% BAC. Which statement is correct?
choices: The driver is over the legal limit for drivers under 21
The driver is legal because the limit is .08% for all drivers
The driver is legal because the under-21 limit is .05%
Only a warning can be issued below .04%
explanation: Ohio's limit for drivers under 21 is .02%, so .03% is over the limit. Operating a vehicle after underage alcohol consumption (OVUAC) can bring a 3-month to 2-year suspension.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: If you refuse a chemical test after an OVI arrest in Ohio and have no prior refusals or OVI convictions, how long is the Administrative License Suspension (ALS)?
explanation: A first refusal brings a one-year ALS that starts immediately. A first test over the limit, by contrast, brings a 90-day ALS.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: A first-time Ohio driver takes a chemical test after an OVI arrest and the result is .08% or higher. How long is the Administrative License Suspension?
explanation: A first test over the limit brings a three-month (90-day) ALS. Refusing the test is punished more harshly: one year for a first refusal.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: A driver refused a chemical test and received an ALS, but was later acquitted of the OVI charge. What happens to the refusal suspension?
explanation: Ohio's manual states that the refusal suspension will stand even if the person is ultimately acquitted of the OVI charge.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: A driver under 21 convicted of operating a vehicle after underage alcohol consumption (OVUAC) in Ohio faces a license suspension of:
explanation: An OVUAC can result in a suspension of three months to two years, plus a remedial driving course, reinstatement fees and retaking the license exam.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: What fine range does Ohio law set for a first OVI conviction?
explanation: For a first OVI offense, ORC 4511.19 requires a fine of not less than $565 and not more than $1,075, along with a 1- to 3-year court license suspension.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.19

prompt: For a first OVI conviction, an Ohio court must suspend the driver's license for a definite period of:
explanation: ORC 4511.19 requires a court suspension of one to three years for a first OVI offense (the court may grant limited privileges).
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.19

prompt: In Ohio, a passenger rides in a car on a public street holding an opened can of beer. Is this legal?
choices: Yes, the open container law applies only to the driver
No, opened containers are illegal for drivers and passengers in a vehicle
Yes, as long as the driver is sober
Yes, if the passenger is 21 or older
explanation: Ohio's open container law (ORC 4301.62) prohibits possessing an opened container of beer or liquor while operating or being a passenger in a motor vehicle on a street or highway.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4301.62

prompt: Under Ohio's ALS rules, how long is the suspension for refusing a chemical test if the driver has one prior refusal or OVI conviction within 10 years?
explanation: Refusal suspensions grow with history: 1 year for a first refusal, 2 years with one prior refusal or OVI/drug conviction, 3 years with two, and 5 years with three or more.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: Under Ohio's distracted driving law, which of these is allowed for a 30-year-old driver while the car is moving?
choices: Holding the phone to type an address into a map app
Reading a text while holding the phone on the steering wheel
Scrolling through a playlist on a handheld phone
Answering a call through the car's hands-free system with a single touch
explanation: Drivers 18 and older may use hands-free features and activate a device with a single touch or swipe, but may not hold or support the phone or manually enter letters, numbers or symbols.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 3

prompt: What is the penalty for a first Ohio distracted driving offense (holding a phone) within two years?
choices: 4 points and up to a $500 fine
2 points and up to a $150 fine
explanation: A first offense in two years brings 2 points and up to a $150 fine. A second brings 3 points and up to $250; a third brings 4 points, up to $500 and a possible 90-day suspension.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 3

prompt: How can an adult Ohio driver avoid the fine and points for a first distracted driving offense?
choices: Show proof of insurance in court
explanation: Ohio's manual says completing a distracted driving course can help avoid the fine and points for a first offense.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 3

prompt: A 30-year-old driver in Ohio picks up the phone to text while stopped at a red traffic light. Under the exceptions in Ohio's manual, this is:
choices: Allowed, because the vehicle is stopped at a traffic light
Illegal, because a phone may never be held in a vehicle
Allowed only if the engine is turned off
Allowed only on roads posted 25 mph or less
explanation: ORC 4511.204(B)(3) and the manual's exceptions allow a driver 18 or older to use a phone while stopped at a traffic signal that is directing traffic to stop. Drivers under 18 do not get this exception: they may not use a device even while sitting at a light.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 3; Ohio Revised Code 4511.204(B)(3)

prompt: A 17-year-old Ohio driver wants to make a hands-free call while driving. Is this allowed?
choices: Yes, hands-free calls are allowed for all ages
Yes, but only after the first 6 months of licensing
Yes, if a passenger 21 or older is present
No, drivers under 18 may not use any electronic device, even hands-free
explanation: Drivers under 18 may not use any electronic device while driving, even hands-free or while sitting at a light. The only exceptions are navigation and emergency calls.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 3

prompt: What is the penalty for an Ohio driver under 18 caught using an electronic device while driving for the first time?
explanation: For drivers under 18, a first violation brings a 60-day suspension and $150 fine; a second brings a 1-year suspension and $300 fine. It is a primary offense.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 3

prompt: A driver under 18 is convicted a second time of using a phone while driving in Ohio. What is the penalty?
explanation: A second violation of the under-18 electronic device ban brings a one-year suspension and a $300 fine.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 3

prompt: What happens to an Ohio distracted driving fine if the violation occurs in a work zone?
choices: It is replaced by a warning
It is tripled and adds 6 points
explanation: Ohio's manual states that distracted driving fines are doubled when the violation occurs in a work zone.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 3

prompt: Ohio's safety belt law requires which occupants to wear a belt whenever an adult is driving, regardless of their age?
choices: Only occupants on highways over 55 mph
The driver and all front-seat occupants
explanation: Ohio requires drivers and front-seat occupants to wear safety belts. Separate child-restraint rules cover children under 16 in any seat, and when the driver is under 18 every occupant must be belted.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 2

prompt: A 17-year-old who has held an Ohio license for over a year drives a car with five safety belts. How many people may ride in the car, including the driver?
choices: Six, if one sits in the cargo area
Any number, if the front seat occupants are belted
No more than five, and all must be belted
Seven, if the trip is under 10 miles
explanation: For drivers under 18, the number of occupants is limited to the number of safety belts originally installed, and all occupants must wear them. (During the first 12 months, a further one non-family passenger limit applies.)
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 2 and p. 12

prompt: In Ohio, a child who is under age 4 or weighs less than 40 pounds must ride in:
choices: The front seat with an adult
explanation: Children under 4 and/or under 40 pounds must be properly restrained in a child safety seat that meets federal safety standards.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: You are driving a 6-year-old who is 4 feet 5 inches tall in Ohio. What restraint is required?
choices: No restraint if seated in the back
explanation: Children at least 4 but under 8 must ride in a booster seat unless they are 4 feet 9 inches or taller.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: Under Ohio's booster seat rule, a 7-year-old who is 4 feet 10 inches tall:
choices: Must ride in a booster seat until age 8
Must ride in a harnessed child safety seat
Must ride in a booster seat until reaching 80 pounds
Is not required to ride in a booster seat
explanation: Children ages 4 to 7 must use a booster seat unless they are 4 feet 9 inches or taller. A child this tall should still be buckled in properly, ideally in the back seat.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: Can an Ohio police officer stop an adult driver only because the driver is not wearing a seat belt?
choices: Yes, it is a primary offense for all drivers
No, the adult seat belt law is secondary enforcement
explanation: ORC 4513.263 forbids stopping a vehicle for the sole purpose of checking or ticketing a seat belt violation. The fine is $30 for the driver and $20 for a front-seat passenger.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4513.263

prompt: What is the minimum age to take the knowledge test and get a temporary instruction permit (TIPIC) in Ohio?
explanation: At 15 years and six months you meet the minimum age for the vision screening and knowledge test needed for a TIPIC.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1

prompt: How is Ohio's driver license knowledge test structured?
explanation: The Ohio knowledge test has 40 multiple-choice questions on motor vehicle regulations and traffic signs, and you must answer 75% (30) correctly.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1; Ohio BMV Temporary Permit page (bmv.ohio.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

prompt: If you fail the Ohio knowledge test in person, when may you retake it?
explanation: The BMV says you must wait at least 24 hours (one day) before retesting. There is no limit on in-person attempts; online testing allows two attempts in six months.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1; Ohio BMV Temporary Permit page (bmv.ohio.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

prompt: After passing the Ohio vision screening and knowledge test, how long do you have to purchase your TIPIC?
explanation: Visit a Deputy Registrar License Agency within 60 days. If you miss that window, you must start over with the vision screening and knowledge test.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1

prompt: How long must an Ohio driver under 18 hold a TIPIC before getting a probationary license?
explanation: Drivers under 18 must hold the temporary instruction permit for at least six months.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1

prompt: How many hours of supervised practice driving must an Ohio driver under 21 log before the driving test?
choices: 50 hours, including at least 10 at night
40 hours, including at least 5 at night
65 hours, including at least 10 at night
30 hours, including at least 8 at night
explanation: Drivers under 21 must log 50 hours with an eligible licensed driver, at least 10 of them at night, in addition to driver education.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1

prompt: What driver education must an Ohio driver under 21 complete at a licensed driver training school?
choices: 30 hours of classroom and 6 hours of driving
8 hours of classroom and 24 hours of driving
24 hours of classroom or online instruction and 8 hours of driving
explanation: The required course is 24 hours of classroom or online instruction plus 8 hours of driving time with a licensed driver training school.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1

prompt: A 15-year-old Ohio permit holder wants to practice driving. Who may sit in the front passenger seat?
choices: Any licensed driver age 18 or older
A parent, guardian, custodian, licensed driving instructor, or person 21+ acting as a parent
explanation: Under 16, the permit holder must have a parent, guardian, custodian, licensed driving instructor, or a person 21 or older acting in loco parentis in the front passenger seat.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1

prompt: A 16-year-old Ohio permit holder wants to drive at 12:30 a.m. with a 25-year-old licensed family friend who is not a parent, guardian, or custodian and is not named on a notarized BMV 2438. Is this allowed?
choices: Yes, any licensed driver 21 or older may supervise at any time
No, from midnight to 6 a.m. the driver must be with a parent, guardian, or custodian
Yes, if the friend has held a license for 3 years
No, permit holders may not drive after sunset
explanation: Permit holders aged 16-17 may drive with any licensed driver 21 or older except from midnight to 6 a.m., when a parent, guardian or custodian with a valid license must accompany them. (The BMV also accepts a licensed adult 21+ named on a notarized form BMV 2438.)
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1; Ohio BMV Temporary Permit page (bmv.ohio.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

prompt: A 19-year-old holds an Ohio TIPIC. Who must accompany them while practicing?
choices: A licensed driver age 21 or older
A licensed driver age 18 or older
No one, because they are an adult
explanation: Permit holders 18 and over may practice driving only when accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 1

prompt: What is the minimum age for an Ohio probationary driver license?
explanation: Ohio may issue a probationary license to a person at least 16 who has held a temporary instruction permit for at least six months. A license without probationary limits requires age 18.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4507.071

prompt: At what age can an Ohio driver get a license with no probationary (under-18) restrictions?
explanation: Ohio does not issue a regular driver license to anyone under 18. Drivers aged 16 and 17 hold a probationary license with curfew, passenger and device limits.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4507.071

prompt: During the first 12 months of holding an Ohio probationary license, a driver under 18 may NOT drive during which hours (unless an exception applies)?
explanation: In the first 12 months, drivers under 18 may not drive from midnight to 6 a.m. unless with a parent or guardian (or a licensed adult 21+ named on a notarized BMV 2438) or traveling to/from work, school or religious events with documentation.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 12

prompt: After the first 12 months of licensing, an Ohio driver who is still under 18 may not drive during which hours (unless an exception applies)?
choices: There is no time restriction after 12 months
explanation: After the first 12 months, the restricted period shrinks to 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. until the driver turns 18.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 12

prompt: During the first 12 months of an Ohio probationary license, how many non-family passengers may the driver carry without a parent or guardian present?
explanation: A new driver under 18 may not drive with more than one non-family member as a passenger unless accompanied by a parent or guardian.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 12

prompt: A 16-year-old with a new Ohio license needs to drive home from a late work shift at 1 a.m. What makes this legal?
choices: Having a friend age 18 in the car
explanation: Driving to or from work during restricted hours is allowed with documentation from the employer (form BMV 2825). A friend age 18 does not qualify; only a parent or guardian (or a licensed adult 21+ named on a notarized BMV 2438) can serve as the escort.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 12; Ohio BMV Temporary Permit page (bmv.ohio.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

prompt: An Ohio driver under 18 is convicted of two moving violations. What happens?
explanation: For drivers under 18, two moving violations result in an automatic three-month suspension; three bring a one-year suspension.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: An Ohio driver under 18 is convicted of three moving violations. What is the automatic suspension?
explanation: Three moving violations by a driver under 18 bring an automatic one-year license suspension.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: How many points within two years lead the Ohio BMV to suspend a driver license?
explanation: Accumulating 12 or more points within two years triggers a 12-point suspension. At 6 points, the BMV sends a warning letter.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: What does the Ohio BMV do when a driver reaches six points within two years?
explanation: At six points in two years, the BMV sends a warning letter; suspension comes at 12 or more points.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: What are Ohio's minimum liability insurance limits?
choices: $25,000 per person / $50,000 per crash / $25,000 property damage
explanation: Ohio requires $25,000 for injury or death of one person, $50,000 for two or more people, and $25,000 for property damage.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: Instead of buying an insurance policy, how else can an Ohioan meet the financial responsibility requirement?
choices: Sign a promise to pay any damages
explanation: Ohio allows a policy, a personal liability bond at the required amounts, or a $30,000 deposit with the Registrar plus proof of no unsatisfied judgments.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: In Ohio, you must show proof of insurance after a crash that causes property damage of more than:
explanation: Proof of financial responsibility must be shown when a driver or owner is involved in a crash with more than $400 in property damage, and also at traffic stops that result in a ticket.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: What is the possible fine for driving under suspension in Ohio?
explanation: Driving under suspension is a first-degree misdemeanor with a fine of up to $1,000 and a possible additional one-year suspension.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 6

prompt: How soon after establishing residency must a new Ohio resident get an Ohio driver license?
explanation: Once you are employed, sign a lease, buy a home or enroll children in school in Ohio, you must get an Ohio license within 30 days.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 13

prompt: When does an Ohio driver license issued to someone under 21 expire?
explanation: A license issued under age 21 expires on the 21st birthday and must be renewed in person; renewal is allowed up to 30 days before.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 12

prompt: A 25-year-old fails the Ohio driving (road or maneuverability) test on the first try and has not taken driver education in the past year. What must they do before retesting?
choices: Complete an Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course
explanation: Applicants 21 or older who fail the skills test must take the Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course before a second attempt, unless they had approved driver education within one year.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 11

prompt: Ohio's "assured clear distance ahead" rule means you must:
choices: Always leave exactly 100 feet behind the vehicle ahead
Drive at the posted limit whenever the road is clear
Never drive faster than allows you to stop within the distance you can see ahead
Keep one car length of space at all speeds
explanation: Regardless of the posted limit, Ohio law prohibits driving faster than lets you stop in the distance available. In poor conditions a reasonable speed may be below the limit.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 4

prompt: Unless posted otherwise, what is Ohio's speed limit in a school zone during recess and while children are arriving or leaving?
explanation: ORC 4511.21 sets 20 mph in school zones during recess and while children are going to or leaving school, where school speed limit signs are posted.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.21

prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on streets within an Ohio city or village (municipal corporation)?
explanation: The prima-facie limit in a municipal corporation is 25 mph, except on alleys (15 mph) and on state routes or through highways outside business districts.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.21

prompt: What is the default speed limit in an alley within an Ohio municipality?
explanation: Ohio law sets 15 mph on alleys within a municipal corporation unless a different limit is posted.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.21

prompt: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on Ohio highways outside cities and villages?
explanation: Highways outside municipal corporations default to 55 mph; some two-lane state routes and rural divided highways may be set at 60 mph.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.21

prompt: Ohio's manual says to keep a minimum following distance of one vehicle length for every 10 mph, or how many seconds behind the vehicle ahead?
explanation: Ohio's manual says to keep at least one vehicle length per 10 mph, or four seconds, between you and the vehicle ahead, and more at night, in bad weather, on slippery roads or behind large vehicles.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 8

prompt: Under Ohio law, driving very slowly is illegal when:
choices: It impedes or blocks the normal and reasonable movement of traffic
You drive more than 5 mph under the posted limit
You drive under 45 mph on any state route
Another driver flashes their headlights at you
explanation: ORC 4511.22 forbids driving so slowly that you impede the normal and reasonable flow of traffic, unless slowing is needed for safety or to obey the law.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.22

prompt: What is the maximum speed limit on Ohio's rural freeways (such as rural interstates)?
explanation: ORC 4511.21 sets 70 mph on all rural freeways. Urban freeways are usually 65 mph or 55 mph in congested areas.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.21

prompt: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on Ohio's rural expressways without traffic signals?
explanation: Ohio law sets 65 mph on rural expressways without traffic signals, 60 mph on rural expressways with signals, and 70 mph on rural freeways.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.21

prompt: On an Ohio road with four or more lanes, which lane should you normally drive in?
choices: The left lane at all times
The right lane, using the lane just right of center to pass and turn left
Any lane, as long as you match traffic speed
explanation: Ohio's manual says to drive in the right lane on roads with four or more lanes and use the lane just right of center to pass and to make left turns.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: How far before a turn must an Ohio driver begin signaling?
explanation: Ohio requires a turn signal at least 100 feet before the intended turn, given by turn signal lights or hand-and-arm signals.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: On a two-lane road with solid double yellow center lines, when may an Ohio driver cross the lines?
choices: To pass any vehicle going under the speed limit
Only at night when no traffic is visible
To turn left into a driveway or to pass a bicycle or slow-moving vehicle when safe
explanation: Passing is prohibited from both directions at a solid double yellow line. Crossing it is allowed only to turn left into a driveway or to pass a slow-moving vehicle such as a bicycle when safe.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: In Ohio, you may cross a solid yellow line to pass a slow-moving vehicle only if that vehicle is traveling at less than:
explanation: You may pass a slow-moving vehicle across a solid yellow line only if it is going less than half the posted limit, you do not exceed the limit while passing, and the oncoming lane is clear.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 9

prompt: How does Ohio law require you to treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not working and no officer is directing traffic?
choices: As a yield sign for the busier road
As a green light for the main road
explanation: When a traffic signal is out, drivers must treat it as a four-way stop unless a law enforcement officer is directing traffic.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 10

prompt: In Ohio, a vehicle displaying this emblem on its rear is traveling at what speed?
explanation: The fluorescent or reflective orange-and-red triangle marks a slow-moving vehicle, such as farm or construction equipment or an animal-drawn vehicle, that travels under 25 mph.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 9

prompt: When may you turn right on a red light in Ohio?
choices: Only where a sign specifically permits it
After slowing down, without stopping, if no one is coming
Only when a green arrow is showing
After a complete stop, yielding to crossing traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it
explanation: Ohio allows right on red after a complete stop unless a sign prohibits it. You must let all crossing traffic and pedestrians clear first.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: In Ohio, a left turn on a red light is allowed only:
choices: From any street onto a one-way street
From a two-way street onto a two-way street after stopping
From the far left lane of a one-way street onto another one-way street
explanation: A left on red is allowed only from the extreme left lane of a one-way street onto another one-way street, after a full stop and unless a sign forbids it.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: You are on a two-way street in Ohio, stopped at a red light, and want to turn left onto a one-way street. May you turn on red?
choices: No, left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
Yes, if no sign prohibits it
Yes, but only between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
explanation: Ohio allows left turns on red only when both streets are one-way. Turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street on red is not allowed.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: An ambulance with flashing lights and siren approaches from behind you on an Ohio street. What must you do?
choices: Pull to the right side of the road and stop until it passes
Speed up to get out of its way
Pull to the left shoulder and stop
explanation: Ohio drivers must quickly and safely pull to the right side of the road and stop, avoid blocking intersections, and stay there until the emergency vehicle passes.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 9

prompt: You are on a divided highway in Ohio and a fire truck with lights and siren is approaching on the opposite side of the median. Must you pull over and stop?
choices: Yes, all traffic in both directions must stop
Yes, but only if you are in the left lane
Only if the fire truck is within 500 feet
No, the stop rule does not apply to emergency vehicles traveling the opposite direction on a divided highway
explanation: Ohio's manual says to stop for an approaching public safety vehicle unless it is traveling in the opposite direction on a divided highway.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: How close may you legally follow a fire truck or other emergency vehicle that is responding to an alarm in Ohio?
explanation: ORC 4511.72 forbids following an emergency or public safety vehicle responding to an alarm closer than 500 feet, or parking within the block where fire apparatus has stopped.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.72

prompt: You approach a tow truck stopped on the shoulder of a multi-lane Ohio highway with its warning lights flashing. What does Ohio's Move Over law require?
choices: Nothing, because the law covers only police vehicles
Move to a lane not next to the truck if safe; otherwise slow down and proceed with caution
Stop behind the tow truck until it leaves
explanation: Ohio's Move Over law requires changing into a lane not adjacent to the stopped vehicle when safe, or slowing down and proceeding with caution if a lane change is unsafe. ORC 4511.213 doubles the usual fine for a violation.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 9; Ohio Revised Code 4511.213

prompt: Which of these vehicles is covered by Ohio's Move Over law when stopped with its warning lights on?
choices: A delivery van with hazard lights
A city bus at a bus stop
A private car with a flat tire
explanation: Ohio's Move Over law covers police, fire and other emergency vehicles, road service vehicles such as tow trucks and snowplows, waste collection vehicles, highway maintenance vehicles and public utilities commission vehicles with warning lights on.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 9

prompt: At an Ohio intersection, there is a stop line painted before the crosswalk. Where must you stop for a red light?
choices: At the edge of the crosswalk farthest from you
In the crosswalk, if no pedestrians are present
Where you can see cross traffic, even past the line
explanation: You must yield to pedestrians entering or in a crosswalk, and if there is a stop line before the crosswalk, the stop line must be obeyed.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 4

prompt: What minimum space does Ohio's manual say to keep when passing a bicycle?
explanation: Maintain a safety zone of at least three feet between your vehicle and a bicycle, slow down when passing, and avoid honking close to a bicyclist.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 9

prompt: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a two-lane Ohio road. How close may you stop to the bus?
explanation: On roads with fewer than four lanes, traffic from both directions must stop at least 10 feet from the front or rear of the bus.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: You are driving on a four-lane Ohio road and meet a stopped school bus with red lights flashing coming from the opposite direction. What must you do?
choices: You are not required to stop
Stop at least 10 feet from the bus
Stop only if children are crossing
explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, only traffic moving in the same direction as the bus must stop. Oncoming traffic may continue with care.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: On a three-lane road (two lanes one way, one lane the other) in Ohio, a school bus stops to load children. Who must stop?
choices: Only traffic in the lane next to the bus
explanation: On a road with fewer than four lanes, all traffic approaching the bus from either direction must stop. Only roads with four or more lanes let oncoming traffic continue.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: A school bus ahead turns on its flashing amber (yellow) lights but has not stopped yet. Under Ohio rules you should:
choices: Stop immediately at least 10 feet away
Pass quickly before the bus stops
Prepare to stop, since you must stop once the bus stops
Ignore the lights; only red lights matter
explanation: Amber lights mean the bus is preparing to stop. Ohio does not require stopping during the amber phase, but you must prepare to stop once the bus comes to a full stop and the red lights flash.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: A stopped Ohio school bus is loading children with red lights flashing, but it has no extended stop arm. Must you stop?
choices: No, a stop arm is required for the law to apply
Only if a child is in the road
Only on roads with four or more lanes
explanation: Ohio's manual states that if there is no stop arm, you are still required to stop.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: What minimum following distance does Ohio's manual recommend behind a motorcycle in ideal conditions at low speed?
explanation: Keep at least three seconds behind a motorcycle at low speeds in ideal conditions, and at least four seconds or more when conditions are less than ideal.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 9

prompt: In Ohio, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
explanation: Ohio prohibits stopping, standing or parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: Ohio law prohibits parking in or within how many feet of an intersection or crosswalk?
explanation: No person may stop, park or stand in or within 20 feet of an intersection or crosswalk.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: How close may you park to a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal on the approach side in Ohio?
explanation: ORC 4511.68 prohibits standing or parking within 30 feet of, and on the approach to, a yield sign, stop sign or traffic signal.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.68

prompt: In Ohio, you may not park within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
explanation: ORC 4511.68 prohibits standing or parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.68

prompt: What parking restriction applies near the driveway entrance of an Ohio fire station?
choices: No parking within 10 feet on the same side only
No parking within 50 feet on either side
No parking within 100 feet on the same side
No parking within 20 feet of the entrance (75 feet on the opposite side when posted)
explanation: Ohio prohibits parking within 20 feet of a fire station driveway entrance and, when signs are posted, within 75 feet of it on the opposite side of the street.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.68

prompt: When parallel parking next to a curb in Ohio, your wheels must be no more than how far from the curb?
explanation: Vehicles must be parked facing the direction of traffic, parallel to and not more than 12 inches from the curb.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: On a one-way street in Ohio, where may you parallel park?
choices: Within 12 inches of either the right or left curb
In the center of the street
explanation: On one-way streets, Ohio allows parking parallel to and not more than 12 inches from either the right or left curb.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: On a cloudy afternoon it starts to drizzle and you turn on your windshield wipers. What does Ohio law require?
explanation: Ohio requires headlights whenever windshield wipers are in use because of precipitation, as well as from sunset to sunrise and in rain, snow or fog.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 7

prompt: Ohio law requires headlights whenever natural light does not let you clearly see objects how far ahead?
explanation: Headlights are required at any time natural light does not make it possible to clearly see objects 1,000 feet ahead.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 7

prompt: According to Ohio's manual, when must you dim your high-beam headlights?
explanation: Use high beams when there are no oncoming vehicles; Ohio law requires you to dim them for approaching traffic. To avoid glare, look toward the right side of the road.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 7

prompt: A train is approaching an Ohio railroad crossing. Where must you stop?
choices: At least 5 feet from the nearest rail
No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the crossing
No closer than 50 feet and no farther than 100 feet
Directly at the crossbuck sign, wherever it is
explanation: Stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the crossing, and wait until the train passes and signals stop.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 5

prompt: When is it legal to use studded tires in Ohio?
explanation: Ohio's manual states that studded tires are legal from November 1 through April 15.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 2

prompt: What can happen if you speed in an Ohio work zone?
choices: A warning only if no workers are present
Nothing extra beyond a normal ticket
Doubled fines and possible jail time
explanation: Speeding in a work zone can bring doubled fines and jail time. Always reduce speed in a work zone, even if no workers are present.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 4

prompt: When may an Ohio driver file a Crash Report (BMV 3303) with the BMV?
choices: Only if police did not come to the scene
Within six months, if there was over $400 damage or an injury and the other driver was uninsured
Within one year, for any crash over $1,000
explanation: Filing is optional: a driver may file form BMV 3303 within six months if there was damage over $400 or personal injury and the other driver or owner had no insurance at the time.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 10

prompt: You hit a parked, unoccupied car in Ohio. What must you do?
choices: Leave, since no one was hurt
Report the crash to police or leave your information at the scene
Wait 30 minutes, then leave if the owner does not return
Report it to the BMV within 30 days only
explanation: If you are in a crash with an unattended vehicle, you must report it to the police or leave the necessary information at the scene.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 10

prompt: Your car breaks down on an Ohio highway. Where does Ohio's manual suggest placing emergency flares?
choices: About 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle
About 1,000 feet ahead of the vehicle
explanation: If possible, place flares about 200 to 300 feet behind your vehicle to give other drivers time to change lanes.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 10

prompt: Under Ohio law, which motorcycle riders must wear a DOT-approved helmet?
choices: Riders under 18, riders in their novice (first-year) period, and permit holders
explanation: ORC 4511.53 requires helmets for riders under 18, novice license or endorsement holders, and permit holders, plus their passengers. Adults past the novice period may ride without one.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.53

prompt: How long is a newly licensed Ohio motorcycle rider considered a novice?
explanation: The BMV considers you a novice for one year, and your license shows the date novice status expires. ORC 4511.53 requires novice riders to wear a helmet.
ref: Ohio BMV, Motorcycle/Motor Scooter page (bmv.ohio.gov); Ohio Revised Code 4511.53(C)(1)

prompt: What eye protection rule applies to motorcycle operators and passengers in Ohio?
choices: All must use safety glasses or another protective eye device
Only riders under 18 need eye protection
Eye protection is needed only at night
A windshield always replaces eye protection
explanation: ORC 4511.53 says no person shall operate or ride as a passenger on a motorcycle without safety glasses or other protective eye device (an enclosed autocycle or cab is excepted).
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.53

prompt: An Ohio motorcycle permit (TIPIC) holder wants to ride after sunset. Is this allowed?
choices: No, permit holders may ride during daylight hours only
Yes, if a licensed rider follows
explanation: Motorcycle TIPIC holders may ride in daylight only, with no passengers, off interstates and congested roads, and must wear a helmet and eye protection.
ref: Ohio BMV, Motorcycle/Motor Scooter page (bmv.ohio.gov); Ohio Revised Code 4511.53(C)(3)(b)

prompt: May an Ohio motorcycle permit holder carry a passenger?
choices: Yes, if the passenger is licensed
Yes, after 30 days on the permit
explanation: Ohio's motorcycle TIPIC restrictions include no passengers.
ref: Ohio BMV, Motorcycle/Motor Scooter page (bmv.ohio.gov)

prompt: Which roads are off-limits to an Ohio motorcycle permit holder?
choices: All roads with a speed limit over 25 mph
None; all public roads are allowed
Interstates and other limited-access or heavily congested roads
explanation: ORC 4511.53(C)(3)(b) bars permit holders from riding on any limited-access highway or heavily congested roadway; the BMV lists this as no riding on interstates or congested roads.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.53(C)(3)(b); Ohio BMV, Motorcycle/Motor Scooter page (bmv.ohio.gov)

prompt: How long is an Ohio motorcycle TIPIC valid?
choices: One year from the date of purchase
explanation: The motorcycle TIPIC is valid for one year from purchase; if it expires, you must start over.
ref: Ohio BMV, Motorcycle/Motor Scooter page (bmv.ohio.gov)

prompt: If you fail any part of the Ohio motorcycle skills test, how long must you wait to retest?
explanation: The BMV requires a one-week wait before retesting after failing any part of the motorcycle skills test.
ref: Ohio BMV, Motorcycle/Motor Scooter page (bmv.ohio.gov)

prompt: For how long does a Motorcycle Ohio Basic Course completion card waive the BMV motorcycle skills test?
explanation: The Motorcycle Ohio Basic Course completion card waives skills testing for 60 days from the date it is issued.
ref: Ohio BMV, Motorcycle/Motor Scooter page (bmv.ohio.gov)

prompt: What must an Ohio rider under 18 complete before getting a motorcycle endorsement or license?
choices: A Motorcycle Ohio safety course, plus probationary driver license requirements
explanation: Riders under 18 must complete a Motorcycle Ohio safety course and meet probationary license requirements, including holding the TIPIC for six months, driver education and 50 logged hours.
ref: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Ohio Motor Vehicle Laws), p. 12; Ohio BMV, Motorcycle/Motor Scooter page (bmv.ohio.gov)

prompt: You are driving through the downtown business district of an Ohio city and see no speed limit signs. What is the speed limit?
explanation: ORC 4511.21 sets 25 mph in a municipal corporation, including its business districts. The 35 mph limit applies only to state routes or through highways outside business districts.
ref: Ohio Revised Code 4511.21(B)(2)-(3)
